"horizontal" or "vertical".
A label drawn in the line. Leave it out for a plain line.
A plain separator has `role="separator"` and `aria-orientation`, like an <l2/>.
A separator with a label has no role. The separator role would make its text presentational, so the label is read as plain text instead.
A vertical separator with a label keeps the text upright and draws the line above and below it.
Align
Built on the Base UI Separator. Renders a <l0/> and accepts its attributes.
Children sit in the middle of the line, with the line filling the space on both sides.
Decorative
Hide the line from screen readers when it is only visual.
Long labels wrap and unbroken strings break, while a short stretch of line stays visible on each side.
Present when the separator has a label.
Separator component for React & shadcn/ui
Start and end follow the reading direction.
Target separators in CSS.
The element that wraps the label.
The label's alignment, when there is a label.
The line is one physical pixel thick on every screen, the same hairline as borders, so it lines up with cards and inputs around it. Space it with the parent's `gap` or a margin.
Use `render` to output a <l1/> where a <l2/> isn't allowed, like inside a paragraph.
Vertical label
Where the label sits along the line.
With `decorative`, it gets `role="none"` and screen readers skip it.
With `orientation="vertical"` the line stretches to the height of its flex row. Outside a flex row, give it a height.
`align` moves the label to the `start` or `end`, which suits section and date headers. Icons are sized to the text.
`decorative` hides a purely visual line from screen readers, so they don't announce a separator between rows that already read well on their own.
